identity.title: Verify C# consumer typed outcome execution example

origin.summary: The 2D plan identifies a P2 external-integration gap: the existing C# consumer example exercises a successful TCP result, but a first-time host developer needs an explicit typed outcome dispatch, awaited completion, correlation checks, and deterministic close boundary.

state.current_summary: PL-0105/2D-051 is resolved in the existing TwoDIntegrationTcpSmoke example. The example now dispatches the four supported v2 terminal pairs, asserts ACK/transaction/run/input/recipe correlation before handling, awaits the explicit run, and disposes the TCP exchange after no pending execution remains. Debug/Release contracts and loopback/regression evidence pass; offline/two-PC/.NET 4.8/hardware/WPF qualification remains outside this slice.

objective.summary: Provide a buildable C# consumer example that uses the existing TwoDIntegrationTcpExchange and IntegrationResultV2 contracts to distinguish Pass, quality Ng, execution error, and cancellation, await completion, assert transaction/run correlation, and leave no pending operation when the exchange is disposed.
constraints: Work only in C:\Git\2D\Dev and keep all generated evidence under D:\OpenVisionLab-TestData\OpenVisionLab_Dev.
Reuse the existing TwoDIntegrationTcpExchange, TwoDIntegrationExchange, shared v2 DTOs, and TCP smoke project; do not add a production protocol, generic message bus, or parallel adapter owner.
Keep library ABI and shared package sources unchanged; this slice may change only the existing C# example/contract and its documentation.
Receiving or discovering a transaction must remain materialization/validation only; only explicit acknowledgement followed by awaited RunAcceptedHandoffAsync may execute.
Do not change the existing v2 message schema, result disposition semantics, or .NET 4.8 support boundary.
Do not modify, stage, commit, or push C:\Git\2D\Original or C:\Git\Shared\OpenVisionLab-Integration-Contracts.
Do not claim actual hardware, two-PC network, offline install, or broad WPF UI qualification from local fake/loopback evidence.

criteria.text: The existing C# consumer example builds and visibly uses awaited explicit acknowledgement/run, a typed four-outcome dispatch, and correlation assertions without relying on a Success bool.
A focused contract maps Completed/Pass, Completed/Ng, Failed/ExecutionError, and Cancelled/Indeterminate to distinct consumer actions and rejects an unclassified status/outcome combination.

The example verifies transaction, handoff, acknowledgement, run, and input/recipe correlation; a mismatch is rejected before consumer handling, and TCP receipt still produces no automatic acknowledgement or run.

The example's await-then-dispose lifecycle leaves no pending execution task, and Debug/Release builds plus the existing result-disposition and TCP smoke regressions pass with the four-outcome guidance recorded in the project documents.

milestones.summary: Confirm the existing example, result-disposition contract, TCP wrapper, and shared DTO owners and document the focused gap.
Add the minimal typed outcome/correlation example surface to the existing C# smoke path without changing production protocol owners.
Run the focused four-outcome, mismatch, receipt-isolation, await/dispose, Debug, and Release checks.
Record owner/call path, usage example, evidence, self-evaluation, and unverified operational boundaries in the durable project documents.

context.summary: The current C# TCP example awaits Ping, Push/Pull, AcknowledgeHandoff, RunAcceptedHandoffAsync, and result delivery, but its visible success handling is limited to Completed/Pass.
The existing result-disposition contract proves SDK step classification, while the consumer example must handle the public IntegrationResultV2 status/outcome pair.
The TCP wrapper owns server lifetime, explicit transfer, ACK, Run, Result read, and IAsyncDisposable cleanup.
This is the shortest route for a contributing developer to understand the example and its typed result contract.

artifacts.summary: Debug/Release build and focused C# consumer example contract evidence.

evidence.observation: The current C# TCP example already uses await using for TwoDIntegrationTcpExchange, awaits explicit Ping/transfer/acknowledgement/RunAcceptedHandoffAsync calls, and checks returned MessageId/RunId/Outcome, but its consumer handling only accepts Completed/Pass. The existing result-disposition contract maps SDK step summaries to typed v2 outcomes but does not expose a public consumer switch. The shared v2 result owns Status, Outcome, RunId, Correlation, Metrics, Evidence, and Error; no new production owner is required.

The existing example's active call path is explicit AcknowledgeHandoff -> awaited RunAcceptedHandoffAsync -> result read -> await using disposal. The new example helper dispatches only Completed/Pass, Completed/Ng, Failed/ExecutionError, and Cancelled/Indeterminate, and AssertCorrelation checks accepted ACK, Transaction/Handoff/Acknowledgement IDs, input/recipe/consumer-build correlation, producer identity, and completed RunId. No production/shared package owner changed.

The focused C# consumer contract exited 0 in Debug and Release. Each report records six passed cases: four distinct typed actions (QualityPass, QualityNg, ExecutionError, Cancelled), an unclassified terminal pair rejected with InvalidState, and a transaction correlation mismatch rejected before dispatch; failed arrays are empty.

The actual loopback C# example exited 0 in Debug and Release with Accepted acknowledgement, Completed/Pass, consumerAction=QualityPass, a non-empty correlated RunId, and receiveDidNotAcknowledge=true, receiveDidNotRun=true, acknowledgeDidNotRun=true. The process completed only after awaiting the explicit Run and the await-using TCP exchange scope closed.

A dirty runtime manifest completed the existing TCP receipt/discovery path but explicit acknowledgement failed closed with InvalidIdentity; both pushed and pulled transactions retained no Acknowledgement or Result. The example did not treat a non-qualified runtime as a quality result.

The existing result-disposition regression passed in Debug and Release with 9/9 cases each. The existing TCP fault/correlation contract passed in Debug and Release, covering delayed partial transfer/reconnect, reversed lifecycle-file order, explicit Result guard, and typed correlationMismatch.

The existing TwoDIntegrationTcpSmoke project built in both Debug and Release with 0 warnings and 0 errors. The clean SourceState identity was produced by the documented fake-git manifest shim for the copied-runtime smoke; this is not evidence that the actual Dev worktree is clean.

The durable report, stable contract, live handoff, documentation map, and reconciliation record identify PL-0105 as the single 2D-051 example owner, preserve the typed mapping and explicit ACK/await/dispose route, link D-drive evidence, and state offline/two-PC/.NET 4.8/hardware/WPF boundaries. The first Debug fault attempt's Release-manifest/Debug-binary identity mismatch and corrected rerun are recorded as a verification configuration issue, not hidden as a product pass.

events.summary: Admit 2D-051 as one existing-example usability slice. Extend the current TCP smoke example with an explicit typed result dispatch and correlation guard, and prove it with a local contract; do not add a production wrapper, change the shared schema, or reopen the already resolved result-disposition/TCP transport owners.
Admitted the single existing-example C# consumer boundary after confirming no duplicate production owner is needed.

Keep TwoDIntegrationTcpExchange and IntegrationResultV2 as the only production owners. Add a small example-only dispatch/correlation helper and a focused contract rather than changing the shared schema or creating another adapter service.
2D-051 acceptance and durable evidence are complete in the existing C# TCP consumer example and shared v2 contract path.
